Market value is the price an informed buyer pays today, determined by a comparative analysis (recent similar sales) — not by the roll. It's this number, and it alone, that should guide a sale price or a purchase offer.
To know the real value of your property, ask for a comparative analysis based on recent sales in the area. It's the only number that counts when it's time to sell or buy.

The municipality applies a comparative factor to bring the roll closer to the market (notably for the Welcome Tax), which clearly shows that the assessment alone isn't the market value. To each number its use: assessment for the taxes, market value to set a price.
To estimate your Welcome Tax, remember that the higher of the price paid and the municipal assessment adjusted by the comparative factor is used. It avoids nasty surprises.

If your assessment seems clearly too high relative to the market, you can contest it within a specific deadline following the filing of a new roll: compare with similar properties, gather proof and file a request for review. Too high an assessment inflates your taxes for years.
Don't miss the review deadline. If your assessment clearly exceeds that of comparable houses, a well-documented challenge can reduce your taxes for years.
